title: Zoo Day Out Tips: Get More From Your Family Visit
description: Zoo day out tips for families: when animals are most active, feeding times and keeper talks, routes for little legs, memberships and saving.
h1: Zoo day out tips for families
intro: A zoo day can mean sleepy animals and tired legs, or a brilliant day full of feeding times and close encounters. These tips help you get the good version.

image.alt: A young boy feeding an animal at a farm park

cardText: Feeding times, routes for little legs and how to save.

blocks.title: Scout’s zoo routine
blocks.text: Grab a map at the entrance, circle the feeding times and keeper talks, then plan your route around them. Animals are usually most active in the morning.
points: Pack layers: zoos are mostly outdoors

sections.html: Animals are often livelier in the cooler morning and late afternoon. Feeding times and keeper talks are the highlights for kids, so build your day around them.
Big zoos involve a lot of walking. Bring a buggy or carrier for under-5s, plan loops rather than out-and-back routes, and use land trains or buses where the zoo has them.

• Book online in advance.
  • Charity zoos often show a ticket with an optional Gift Aid donation. You can usually choose the standard ticket.
  • Memberships suit local families who visit more than twice a year.
  • Some zoos appear on the rail 2FOR1 list.
Many zoos have indoor houses (reptiles, butterflies, nocturnal animals). Or swap to an aquarium. See zoos and aquariums and rainy day ideas.

faqs.q: What time are animals most active at the zoo?
faqs.a: Many animals are more active in the morning and late afternoon, when it’s cooler. Feeding times are also a great time to see them moving.
